newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia proposes jointly developing disputed isles.
newsitem.headline: Russia proposes jointly developing disputed isles.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov formally proposed on Friday that Russia and Japan jointly develop the islands at the heart of a long dispute between them, Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) officials said.
Primakov's proposal came in his talks with former prime minister Yasuhiro Nakasone and LDP policy chief Taku Yamazaki, said the officials from Japan's ruling party.

It was the first time Russia had formally proposed joint development of the islands, called the Southern Kuriles by Moscow and the Northern Territories by Tokyo. The chain of islands lie just off Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido.

Ownership of the islands, which the former Soviet Union took over at the end of World War two, has stopped Tokyo and Moscow from formally signing a World War Two peace treaty and stood in the way of major Japanese aid to Russia.
Before Primakov arrived in Japan on Thursday, Japanese government officials had said they would listen to a joint development proposal if it did not hurt Japan's claim over the islands.
"I would like to propose the joint development of the four islands, without damaging the basic positions of both Russia and Japan," LDP officials quoted Primakov as telling Nakasone and Yamazaki.
